newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open a bit firmer, eye on weekend.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open a bit firmer, eye on weekend.

text.p: Canadian bonds firmed slightly at Friday's open, pausing after the week's volatility as investors tidied their portfolios ahead of the weekend.

"People are going to clean up their books, going into the weekend," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research at Midland Walwyn Capital. He forecast that bonds would trade close to the present level for the rest of the day.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.26 to C$120.45 to yield 6.447 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 6/32 to yield 6.43 percent and the spread between the bonds narrowed to two basis points from three at Thursday's close.
"We're essentially keeping pace with the U.S.," said Lehman Brothers economist Michael Gregory.

The U.S. market was firmer on Friday after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gave signs this week that U.S. short-term interest rates would remain steady for the time being. "I think it's lingering positives from Greenspan's testimony earlier this week," Gregory said.
"A lot of cash out there," Gregory added.

Canada's short end is underperforming the U.S. because investors are concerned that the Canadian dollar could weaken further, forcing the Bank of Canada to step in with an interest rate hike, Gregory said.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond dipped C$0.01 to reach C$109.74 to yield 5.928 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 3/32 to yield 6.15 percent and the negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 22 basis points from 24 at Thursday's close.
